The studio smelled of lavender and suppressed judgment. Jim, a man whose idea of stretching was reaching for the remote without standing up, had intended to join "Gentle Flow for Beginners." Instead, he had wandered into "Advanced Ashtanga: The Pain Cave."

The instructor, a woman named Serenity who looked like she was carved from marble and patience, clapped her hands once. The sound was like a gunshot in a library.

"Find your center," she whispered. "And then let it go."

Jim found his center. It was located somewhere between his knees and his dignity.

"Downward Dog," Serenity commanded.

Jim attempted to become a dog. He became more of a confused giraffe that had fallen off a ladder. His neck, naturally long, was the only part of him that seemed to understand the geometry of the pose. The rest of him was a tangled knot of limbs and anxiety.

"Engage your core," Serenity said, gliding past him. She didn't even look at him. She just radiated judgment.

Jim engaged his core. It felt like he was trying to suck in a beach ball. He held the pose, his face turning a shade of red that matched the studio’s accent wall. He was sweating profusely. The silence in the room was heavy, broken only by the rhythmic breathing of twelve yogis who were currently meditating on their own superiority.

Then, Jim shifted his weight.

It wasn't a graceful shift. It was a desperate, microscopic adjustment to relieve the pressure on his left glute. But in the confined space of his own body, it was a seismic event.

*Prrrrt.*

It was a short, sharp sound. Like a deflating whoopee cushion.

The class didn't stop. They were too disciplined. But the air changed. The zen was cracked.

Jim froze. His brain screamed, *Don't move. Don't breathe. Don't exist.*

But the universe, in its infinite cruelty, was not done with him.

*Prrrrt-toot.*

This one was longer. It had a trailing edge. It echoed off the mirrored walls.

Serenity stopped mid-pose. She turned her head slowly, like an owl spotting a particularly rude field mouse. Her eyes locked onto Jim. Jim’s eyes locked onto the floor, wishing he could dissolve into the mat.

"Jim," Serenity said
